Tiszaeszlar Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Vörösmarty utca 45, Hungary

Not demolished. Tiszaeszlár is infamous as the site of an 1882 blood libel case, in which local Jews were falsely accused of ritually murdering a missing girl, Eszter Solymosi, whose body was later found to have drowned; all the accused were eventually acquitted after a lengthy trial, but the surrounding antisemitic backlash led Győző Istóczy to found Hungary's first explicitly antisemitic political party later that year, which went on to win parliamentary seats in 1884 and 1887. This cemetery, established by 1864, served an already-small community that by 1885 had merged administratively with the Jewish community of nearby Tiszalök and, before its 1944 deportation, no longer employed its own rabbi or collected communal taxes. None of the deportees are known to have returned to reestablish the community, and the town's synagogue was demolished in the 1950s.
